trial.label: No risk
trial.title: Try the whole thing free for 14 days
trial.subtitle: Every account starts with a 14-day free trial. Not a demo account, not a limited sandbox — the real thing, with your own leads in it.

items.title: Full access from day one
items.body: Pipelines, automations, the calendar, the funnels, the mobile app. You're evaluating what you'd actually be paying for, not a stripped-down preview of it.

items.title: Cancel before day 14 and that's it
items.body: If it isn't for you, you cancel and walk away. No contract to get out of, no phone call to sit through. If you stay, it's $97 a month.

items.title: Use your setup call inside the trial
items.body: This is the part most agents miss. Book the call in your first few days and you spend the trial judging a system that's already built for your business — not an empty account you never got around to configuring.

trial.note: Most people who quit a CRM quit because they never finished setting it up. That's exactly what the setup call is for, and why it belongs inside the trial rather than after it.

problem.label: Sound familiar?
problem.title: The problem was never the leads
problem.subtitle: It's what happens to them after they come in.

items.title: Your leads live in three places
items.body: Facebook messages, your phone's notes app, and a spreadsheet you stopped updating in March.

items.title: The follow-up never happens
items.body: You meant to call back on day three. It's day thirty, and they already bought from the agent who did.

items.title: You're paying for five tools
items.body: One for texting, one for the calendar, one for the funnel, one for email, one for forms. None of them talk to each other.

items.title: You can't tell what's working
items.body: You know you wrote business last month. You don't know which ad, post, or referral actually produced it.

features.label: What you get
features.title: Everything under one login
features.subtitle: This isn't a lead vendor or a dialer. It's the whole back office — the place your leads land, get worked, and turn into appointments.

items.title: Every lead in one pipeline
items.body: Drag a contact from New to Quoted to Submitted. One board tells you what's actually in play this week.

items.title: Follow-up that runs itself
items.body: Text, email, and voicemail sequences you build once. They fire on day 1, day 3, and day 30 whether you remember or not.

items.title: One inbox for everything
items.body: Texts, emails, Facebook and Instagram messages, and WhatsApp land in the same thread as the rest of that person's history.

items.title: A calendar people can book
items.body: Send a link, they pick a time, it lands on your calendar with the reminders that cut your no-shows.

items.title: Funnels, forms, and websites
items.body: Build the quote page, the lead form, and the thank-you page inside the same tool that stores the lead.

items.title: Reviews and reputation
items.body: Ask for the Google review right after the policy is issued — the one moment they actually want to leave you one.

items.title: Reporting you'll actually read
items.body: Where leads came from, what they cost, and which source turned into issued business instead of noise.

items.title: It runs from your phone
items.body: Reply between appointments, from the car, from the kitchen table. The mobile app is the same system, not a stripped-down version.

replaces.label: Do the math
replaces.title: Count what you're paying for right now
replaces.body: Most agents I talk to are subscribed to four or five of these separately. Agent CRM does all of it under one login.
replaces.footnote: Fewer subscriptions is the small win. The big one is that they finally talk to each other.

isaac.label: Who's telling you this
isaac.name: Isaac Orraiz
isaac.role: Licensed insurance agent · Isaac Plans Insurance
isaac.quote: I'm not a software guy. I'm a producing agent who got tired of losing people in a spreadsheet. I run ACA, final expense, IUL, dental, and supplemental business through this one account, in English and Spanish — and on our call I'll show you exactly how it's wired.

items.question: What exactly is Agent CRM?
items.answer: An all-in-one platform where an agent keeps leads, follow-up, calendars, funnels, conversations, and reporting under one login — instead of five separate subscriptions that don't talk to each other.

items.question: Do I need to be technical?
items.answer: No. That's the entire point of the setup call. I build the first version with you, and you learn the system by watching your own account get built.

items.question: Does it cost more through your link?
items.answer: No — it's $97 a month either way. Sign up through my link or go straight to Agent CRM yourself and you pay exactly the same. Agent CRM pays me a referral commission at no additional cost to you, and that commission is what pays for the time I spend setting you up. Going direct just means you pay the same $97 and get none of that.

items.question: I'm brand new. Is it too early for a CRM?
items.answer: It's the cheapest possible time. Building the habit of one place for every lead costs you nothing when you have thirty contacts, and it's a nightmare to untangle when you have three thousand.

items.question: What lines of business does it work for?
items.answer: Any of them. I run ACA, final expense, IUL, dental and vision, hospital indemnity, and short-term medical through the same account.

items.question: I already use another CRM. Can I switch?
items.answer: Yes, and you can run both while you migrate. Bring it up on the setup call and we'll map out what moves first so nothing falls through the cracks.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to try it?
items.answer: No. Every account starts with a 14-day free trial, so you can work your own leads through the system before you pay for it. Cancel before the trial ends and you aren't charged.

items.question: What happens at the end of the 14 days?
items.answer: If you keep it, your plan simply begins. If it isn't for you, cancel before the trial is up and that's the end of it — there's no contract and nothing to negotiate your way out of.

items.question: How do I claim the setup call and the group?
items.answer: Open your account through the button on this page, then send me your confirmation. Or use the form below and I'll reach out to you.
